summary: Urn haircap is a moss found on gravelly banks, disturbed ground, sandy watersides and rock fissures across parts of Europe, North America and Asia. Its wine-red stems and bluish-green cast help distinguish it. Vertical stacks of cells on the leaves add photosynthetic tissue, aid gas exchange and help resist drying. Its capsules mature in autumn, then release spores gradually through small openings between specialized teeth, often beginning the following spring.

Yellow horned poppy is a summer-flowering coastal plant native to Europe, northern Africa, Macaronesia and temperate western Asia. It grows on shingle, beaches, dunes and cliff tops. Waxy, bluish-grey leaves retain water, while bright yellow or orange flowers are followed by unusually long, horn-shaped capsules that split into two chambers to expose the seeds. The plant releases foul-smelling orange sap when cut, and the supplied account reports every part as toxic if eaten.

details.effect: a wide range of symptoms, including respiratory failure and death

summary: Finger lime is a thorny rainforest shrub or small tree native to the coastal border region of Queensland and New South Wales. Its narrow, slightly curved fruits contain separate globular juice vesicles that burst with an acidic, lime-like flavour. The fresh vesicles are used in garnishes and recipes, while the fruit is also made into marmalade and pickles and the dried peel is used as a spice. The species is now grown commercially in Australia.

details.use: eaten fresh as a garnish or added to recipes

reviewFlags: The source describes unresolved confusion and synonymy between Trithrinax acanthocoma and T. brasiliensis, so species-level attribution needs review.

summary: Western redbud is a deciduous shrub or small tree found mainly in Oregon and northern California, where it grows in foothill woodland, chaparral and dry streamside canyons. Bright pink or magenta flowers cover its branches before the leaves emerge, and dry seed pods remain through winter. Its flowers feed native insects and hummingbirds, leafcutter bees harvest its leaves, and Indigenous Californians use and manage its young twigs for basketry.

Drooping sheoak is a small tree endemic to south-eastern Australia. Its long hanging branchlets carry leaves reduced to tiny scale-like teeth, and its woody cones contain winged seeds. It grows in grassy woodland, on rocky coasts and on dry inland ridges. Aboriginal Australians have made tools such as boomerangs from its timber, while on Kangaroo Island its seeds are the preferred food of the glossy black cockatoo.

details.use: chewed to stimulate saliva and relieve severe thirst

summary: Prostrate capeweed is a low, rosette-forming plant native to Namibia and South Africa's Cape Provinces. Creeping stolons create a ground-hugging mat of pale green, silvery leaves and bright yellow, daisy-like flowers. The supplied accounts distinguish an infertile form cultivated as ground cover from reports of a fertile form that spreads rapidly in disturbed ground. Introduced populations in California and Australia are described as invasive and difficult to control.
reviewFlags: The source conflicts over whether Arctotheca prostrata is sterile or includes a fertile invasive form.

summary: Rough-leaved hydrangea is a large deciduous shrub native to dense forests from the Himalayas across southern China to Taiwan. Its broad leaves have a downy, rough-textured underside, while late-summer flower heads combine fertile flowers with larger sterile florets around the edge. Flower colour varies with soil chemistry: acidic soil and greater uptake of soluble aluminium are associated with bluer flowers, while more alkaline conditions produce pinker shades.

Wild candytuft is an annual flowering plant native to parts of western and central Europe, where it favours warm, sunny sites with calcium-rich soil. Its white or pale-violet flowers have four conspicuously unequal petals. The two outer petals become nearly twice as long as the sepals because a gene called IaTCP1 is activated at a different time, prompting extra cell growth in those petals.

Peucedanum oreoselinum is a flowering plant in the carrot family, native to mainland Portugal and distributed more widely in Europe. In Portugal it is confined to high ground in the north-east, growing along woodland edges and in clearings. A national assessment classified it as Vulnerable because only three locations were identified and its occupied area was small; road-verge management and the tiny size of two populations were among the concerns recorded.

Spanish fir is an evergreen conifer native to mountain ranges in southern Spain and northern Morocco. Its needles radiate around the shoots and appear pale blue-green because broad bands of whitish wax cover both sides. The upright cones change from green or pinkish purple as they mature, then break apart to release winged seeds. Conservation and reforestation have increased its abundance, but the source still records threats from fire, erosion, development and heavy visitor pressure.

Mediterranean juniper is a shrub or small tree native across the Mediterranean and Arabian Peninsula, favouring sandy, limestone or volcanic soils. Its adult leaves lie scale-like against the twigs, and it produces pollen in autumn rather than spring. Long treated as part of Juniperus phoenicea, it was supported as a separate species by a DNA study published in 2013; Canary Island plants formerly included with it were separated as Juniperus canariensis in 2023.

Santa Catalina Island currant is a low perennial shrub native to the coasts and islands of southern California and Baja California. Long reddish stems spread horizontally beneath glossy, leathery leaves whose glands release a sticky, citrus-scented sap. Deep red flowers open from late winter into early spring, drawing hummingbirds and insects; small red fruits follow later in spring and attract birds. It grows in partly shaded canyons, coastal scrub, foggy chaparral and some island pine groves.

Cow's horn plant is a succulent shrub native to parts of South Africa, Mozambique and Eswatini. Its paired spines resemble a bull's horns, giving the species its scientific name. Small leaves appear between the spines and later fall, leaving the thick, three-angled stems to perform most photosynthesis. The plant grows in dry mixed forest, on granite slopes and among rocks, and its conspicuous ripe fruit opens with a pop.
Valerianella eriocarpa is a flowering plant in the valerian family. The supplied account records both of its listed varieties as native to mainland Portugal.
Sesamoides purpurascens is a flowering plant in the mignonette family. The supplied account records the species as present and native in mainland Portugal.

Lusterleaf holly is an evergreen tree native to southern Japan and eastern and southern China, where it grows in broadleaf forests. Its glossy, leathery leaves are among the largest found in hollies and have serrated edges without spines. Male and female flowers grow on separate trees, and dense clusters of fruit ripen from orange-red to dark red in winter. The leaves are also infused to make a drink known as bitter nail tea.
Nonea vesicaria is a flowering plant in the borage family. The supplied account records the species as present and native in mainland Portugal.

Lesser duckweed is a tiny floating plant of quiet ponds and lagoons, with green fronds generally no more than six millimetres long. Its rapid growth and nutrient absorption make it useful in aquariums for taking up excess nutrients and shading fish. Those same traits, combined with accidental releases, have helped it establish beyond its original range, including in waterways in Eurasia, Africa, South America and parts of Oceania.

Egyptian crowfoot grass is a creeping grass native to Africa and Asia. It generally grows on heavy soils in damp places and produces upright shoots about 30 centimetres tall. Outside its native range, including in parts of the United States, it is regarded as a weed and invasive species.

summary: Trailing iceplant is a flowering plant in the ice-plant family, native to South Africa's Cape Provinces. Both the unimproved species and cultivars in apricot, orange, peach, purple and red colour selections are commercially available.

Sandveld brightfig is a succulent endemic to South Africa's Western Cape, occurring from Redelinghuys through the Cape Peninsula and Agulhas Plain as part of the fynbos. The supplied account reports that half of its habitat has been lost to coastal and urban development, crop cultivation and invasive plants, with rooibos and potato fields replacing large areas in the Sandveld.
reviewFlags: The reported 50% habitat loss is not dated in the supplied source.

summary: Phyllarthron bojerianum is a flowering shrub or tree endemic to Madagascar. It grows 10 to 15 metres tall and is widespread across the island, occupying habitats from humid lowland and coastal forests to dry deciduous and montane forests over an elevation range of 5 to 2,180 metres.

reviewFlags: The supplied text provides only family-level identity and no narrative traits, origin, ecology or uses.

summary: Calliandra tweediei is a flowering plant in the legume family, native to the Atlantic Forest of south-eastern Brazil.
